events.name: Goodbye Politicians, Hello Democracy Film Screening
events.description:
What if you randomly selected average Americans and had them deliberate on what to do about a complex, contentious political issue? Well in fall of 2020, during the height of COVID lockdowns, that's exactly what Adam Cronkite did. 30 randomly selected Michiganders, stratified by demographics, gathered on Zoom for six weeks to come up with a set of recommendations for the state government on what to do about COVID. These deliberations, plus the personal diaries recorded by these delegates, became the film Goodbye Politicians, Hello Democracy.
This film explores the idea of "sortition democracy," or government by bodies of randomly selected citizens. We'll begin with a brief primer, then watch the 75 minute film, and follow up with a discussion.

events.name: Builders NYC: Dev Talk LIVE
events.description:
Dev Talk LIVE
Come hear what NYC builders are actually working on.
Dev Talk LIVE brings together a small lineup of developers, founders, and builders to showcase what they’ve built, tell the story behind it, and break down the technical and product decisions that got them there.
Each featured builder gets the floor to take us inside their project: what they set out to build, the problems they ran into, the technology behind it, what changed along the way, and what they learned from shipping it. Then we open things up for questions and conversation with the room.
No endless panels. No surface-level startup pitches. No pretending everything went perfectly.
Just builders talking builds.
We’ll have roughly 90–95 minutes of featured Dev Talks, with plenty of breathing room between sessions and time before and after to meet other developers, founders, creatives, and technologists from around NYC.
Schedule
6:30 PM — Doors Open + Meet the Community
7:00 PM — Dev Talk LIVE Begins
8:35 PM — Talks Wrap
8:35–9:00 PM — Hang Out, Meet the Speakers + Networking
Whether you’re working on your own product, looking for inspiration, interested in how other people approach building, or just want to meet more people making cool things in NYC, come through.
Bring your questions. Meet some builders. Leave with something to think about.
You can connect with us here: https://linktr.ee/builders.nyc

events.name: Escaping Flatland NYC IRL v4
events.description:
Welcome to the fourth iteration of Escaping Flatland IRL NYC—a meetup group that shares an interest in Henrik Karlsson's Substack blog on attention, beauty, and living intentionally.
At this event, we'll have a mixture of open-ended mingling and more structured discussion around two of his essays. 

The selected essays for the event are "Almost anything you give sustained attention to will begin to loop on itself and bloom" and "Looking for Alice". I'm suspecting the latter is a fan-favorite...

Feel free to bring snacks, drinks, or whatever else you'd like!
Special thanks to Fractal Tech for lending us the space for the event. I strongly encourage you all to check out their other events; they truly are a wonderful community!

events.name: AI Builders Week 4: RAG, Vector Search & Context Memory
events.description:
Your model only knows what you give it. This session is about giving it the right things: chunking documents so they stay meaningful, generating embeddings, and running vector search that actually grounds your answers in real sources. Then context memory: what to keep, what to summarize, and what to throw away so your agent stays sharp over long conversations without blowing up your token bill.
You'll leave with a working local RAG pipeline you can plug into your fellowship project.
Some coding experience needed. This is about applied engineering, not starting from scratch.
Part of the AI Architect Fellowship, a free program from 3percentclub for underrepresented builders in NYC.
Joining virtually? Live stream: https://us06web.zoom.us/s/84280401788
Applying to the fellowship gets you:
Access to our Google Classroom for labs and coursework

events.name: AI Builders Week 5: Privacy & Security Controls
events.description:
What happens to the data an agent sends, stores, and returns? We’ll look at Zero Data Retention, endpoint controls, self-hosting options, and how to handle personal information in a system people may rely on.
You’ll examine the privacy and security choices for your own project as cross-track pods form with Citizens.
Some coding experience needed. This is about applied engineering, not starting from scratch.
